subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The First Life Insurance Policies
description: One-minute skill: The First Life Insurance Policies.

hook.text: In 1583, a London man insured his own life for one year. He died within the year. The insurer paid.

buildup.text: Early life insurance was basically gambling. People bet on when strangers would die.

discovery.text: The Gambling Act of 1774 required an 'insurable interest' — you had to care if the person lived.

twist.text: Without that law, life insurance would have stayed a morbid betting market on strangers' deaths.

climax.text: Regulation turned life insurance from a death bet into a family safety net.

punchline.text: From death bets to safety nets. Law made it real.

quiz.question: What did the Gambling Act of 1774 require for life insurance?
options: An insurable interest in the person covered
Approval by Parliament for each policy
Coverage only for people over forty
